summary: Kisatchie NF site in Natchitoches Parish, LA: CCC-built steel tower removed in 1983 to Fort Sill, Oklahoma; the byway guide lists the site as a stop; no remains described.

facts.design: 100' steel tower with 11'x11' steel cab and 3' walkway all around
facts.status_note: Removed in 1983 to Fort Sill, Oklahoma, per the register; no source we read describes what remains on the Louisiana site.

access.note: Inferred from the Longleaf Trail guide listing the site as a stop; no visitor rules or site condition are described

visit.trail_note: The Longleaf Trail guide lists the Red Dirt Fire Tower Site as a stop; it says nothing about what remains

events.note: Built by CCC Company 1491, per the register. The byway guide says the site dates back to 1936 (see resolved_conflicts)
Removed because it was no longer needed; replaced by a forest-wide system of aerial detection

corrections.why: The register describes a 100-foot steel tower (30.5 m). The 34.1 m figure matches the 112 feet in the 1941 Coast and Geodetic Survey description, which conflicts with the register. Editor should confirm which figure to show.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register: 100-foot tower (30.5 m). The 1941 survey description, copied on the Forest Lookouts site: about 112 feet. The story uses the register's 100 feet and reports the survey figure.
Register: built 1937 by CCC Company 1491. The Longleaf Trail guide: the site dates back to 1936. The story uses 1937 and reports the guide's date.

sources.title: Red Dirt Lookout Site, Former Fire Lookout Sites Register
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites Register (Forest Fire Lookout Association)

sources.title: Longleaf Trail Scenic Byway guide, Kisatchie Ranger District

notes_for_editor: Height (100 ft in the register, about 112 ft in the 1941 survey) and build year (1937 in the register, 1936 in the byway guide) disagree. The move to Fort Sill, Oklahoma comes only from the register; we did not find a second source for it. Public access is inferred from the byway guide listing the site as a stop, not from a visitor rule. The guide's publication date was not visible in what we read.
